evals.prompt: Audit the state machines under /tmp/eval-state-machine-invariants-0/ and tell me whether any bugs were found.
evals.description: Happy path: one clean YAML state machine in the working directory. The skill should discover it, parse and flatten through the pipeline, run the five checks, and report zero findings.
evals.setup: mkdir -p /tmp/eval-state-machine-invariants-0 && cd /tmp/eval-state-machine-invariants-0 && printf '%s\n' 'id: order' 'initial: pending' 'final: [delivered, cancelled]' 'events: [pay, ship, deliver, cancel]' 'transitions:' '  - {from: pending, event: pay,     to: paid}' '  - {from: paid,    event: ship,    to: shipped}' '  - {from: shipped, event: deliver, to: delivered}' '  - {from: pending, event: cancel,  to: cancelled}' '  - {from: paid,    event: cancel,  to: cancelled}' > order.fsm.yaml && git init -q && git add . && git commit -q -m init
evals.expected_output: The skill discovers `order.fsm.yaml`, normalises it through `normalize_yaml.py`, flattens through `flatten.py` (no-op for a flat machine), runs the five invariant checks via `check_invariants.py`, and produces a markdown report summarising zero findings across one analysed spec. A `state-machine-invariants-report.json` sidecar is written to the working directory; an `order.fsm.ir.json` sidecar is written next to the input YAML.

assertions.text: The markdown report contains 'Analysed 1 spec(s).' and 'Findings: 0'.
The markdown report contains a line for `order.fsm.yaml` marked with ✓ and the text 'no findings'.
A file `/tmp/eval-state-machine-invariants-0/order.fsm.ir.json` exists after the run.
A file `state-machine-invariants-report.json` exists in the working directory after the run, and its `analyzed` array contains the order.fsm.yaml path.

evals.prompt: Find bugs in the state machine under /tmp/eval-state-machine-invariants-1/ and include the categorial / algebraic interpretation of each finding.
evals.description: All five v1 invariants fire on a single buggy YAML: an unreachable state, a deadlock, a literally-false guard, two identical `expr` guards on the same (state, event), and a declared-but-unused event. The skill should report exactly five findings — one per invariant — and surface the math one-liners under `--with-math`.
evals.setup: mkdir -p /tmp/eval-state-machine-invariants-1 && cd /tmp/eval-state-machine-invariants-1 && printf '%s\n' 'id: order' 'initial: pending' 'final: [delivered, cancelled]' 'states: [pending, paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, abandoned]' 'events: [pay, ship, deliver, cancel, refund]' 'transitions:' '  - {from: pending, event: pay,     to: paid}' '  - {from: paid,    event: ship,    to: shipped}' '  - {from: shipped, event: deliver, to: delivered}' '  - {from: pending, event: cancel,  to: cancelled}' '  - {from: paid,    event: cancel,  to: cancelled, guard: "ctx.allow"}' '  - {from: paid,    event: cancel,  to: cancelled, guard: "ctx.allow"}' '  - {from: paid,    event: cancel,  to: cancelled, guard: false}' > order.fsm.yaml && git init -q && git add . && git commit -q -m init
evals.expected_output: The report enumerates five distinct findings — one reachability, one deadlock, one dead-transition, one overlapping-guards, one unused-event — and each finding includes a `[Math: …]` line in categorial / algebraic vocabulary (orbit, sink, image of a projection, non-functional relation).

assertions.text: The markdown report contains an unreachable-state finding mentioning `abandoned`.
The markdown report contains a deadlock finding mentioning `abandoned`.
The markdown report contains a dead-transition finding referencing the `cancel` event on `paid` with a `false` guard.
The markdown report contains an overlapping-guards finding on `(paid, cancel)` whose detail mentions identical `ctx.allow` guards.
The markdown report contains an unused-event finding for `refund`.
Every finding in the markdown report is followed by a line beginning with '[Math:'.

evals.prompt: Run the state-machine-invariants audit on /tmp/eval-state-machine-invariants-2/. Then run it again. Confirm both runs produced the same findings and that the source YAML was not modified.
evals.description: Idempotent re-run: the skill must produce the same findings on a second invocation against the same input, and must not mutate the user's source YAML between runs (only the IR sidecar and the report JSON are written).
evals.setup: mkdir -p /tmp/eval-state-machine-invariants-2 && cd /tmp/eval-state-machine-invariants-2 && printf '%s\n' 'id: small' 'initial: a' 'events: [X, Y]' 'transitions:' '  - {from: a, event: X, to: b}' '  - {from: b, event: X, to: a}' > small.fsm.yaml && cp small.fsm.yaml small.fsm.yaml.expected && git init -q && git add . && git commit -q -m init
evals.expected_output: Two reports are produced. The set of findings (each finding's `invariant`, `summary`, and `location` fields) is identical between the two runs. The source file `small.fsm.yaml` is byte-identical to `small.fsm.yaml.expected` after both runs; the IR sidecar `small.fsm.ir.json` and the report JSON may be rewritten but their *content* is stable.

assertions.text: After both runs, `/tmp/eval-state-machine-invariants-2/small.fsm.yaml` is byte-identical to the `small.fsm.yaml.expected` snapshot taken before the first run.
The set of findings (by `invariant` and `summary`) is the same between the first and second run.
The contents of `/tmp/eval-state-machine-invariants-2/small.fsm.ir.json` after the second run match the contents after the first run.

evals.prompt: Check the XState machine at /tmp/eval-state-machine-invariants-3/auth.ts for unreachable states or overlapping guards.
evals.description: XState input path: the skill must use `extract-xstate.cjs` (or the Python fallback if Node is unavailable) to lift the `createMachine(...)` config into the IR, then run the five checks. The fixture has two identical guards on `(loggedOut, SUBMIT)` so the overlap check fires.
evals.setup: mkdir -p /tmp/eval-state-machine-invariants-3 && cd /tmp/eval-state-machine-invariants-3 && printf '%s\n' "import { createMachine } from 'xstate';" "export const m = createMachine({" "  id: 'auth'," "  initial: 'loggedOut'," "  states: {" "    loggedOut: {" "      on: {" "        SUBMIT: [" "          { target: 'adminFlow',    cond: 'isAdmin' }," "          { target: 'standardFlow', cond: 'isAdmin' }" "        ]" "      }" "    }," "    adminFlow:    { type: 'final' }," "    standardFlow: { type: 'final' }" "  }" "});" > auth.ts && git init -q && git add . && git commit -q -m init
evals.expected_output: The skill recognises `auth.ts` as an XState file, invokes `extract-xstate.cjs`, writes `auth.fsm.ir.json` next to the source, runs the checks, and reports at least one overlapping-guards finding citing `isAdmin` as the shared guard.

assertions.text: A file `/tmp/eval-state-machine-invariants-3/auth.fsm.ir.json` exists after the run and was produced by the XState extractor (the IR's `id` field is `auth`).
The markdown report contains an overlapping-guards finding on `(loggedOut, SUBMIT)` whose detail mentions `isAdmin`.
Findings in the report and JSON sidecar reference `auth.ts` (not the `.fsm.ir.json` sidecar) as the spec path.

evals.prompt: Audit the state machines under /tmp/eval-state-machine-invariants-4/ and tell me which ones could not be analysed and why.
evals.description: Mixed result: one analysable YAML alongside a malformed one (missing required `initial` and `transitions`). The skill must analyse the valid one, record the malformed one as skipped with a reason, and surface the skip in the report's 'skipped' section.
evals.setup: mkdir -p /tmp/eval-state-machine-invariants-4 && cd /tmp/eval-state-machine-invariants-4 && printf '%s\n' 'id: good' 'initial: a' 'events: [X]' 'transitions:' '  - {from: a, event: X, to: b}' '  - {from: b, event: X, to: a}' > good.fsm.yaml && printf '%s\n' 'id: broken' 'states: [a, b]' > broken.fsm.yaml && git init -q && git add . && git commit -q -m init
evals.expected_output: The report shows `good.fsm.yaml` analysed (with whatever findings the checks produce — at minimum, the deadlock check is satisfied trivially since the machine has no final states declared) and lists `broken.fsm.yaml` under the skipped section with a reason mentioning missing required keys.

assertions.text: The markdown report lists `good.fsm.yaml` as analysed (either with ✓ no findings or with one or more findings, but not under the skipped section).
The markdown report contains a `⚠ skipped` entry for `broken.fsm.yaml`, and the reason mentions a missing required key (e.g. `initial` or `transitions`).
The report's summary line shows `Skipped: 1 spec(s).`
